summary: After two iterations, the solution scores a perfect 100/100 consistently (3/3 runs in iter-2, building on 4/5 in iter-1). The core algorithm—tree DP with depth-parity anti-oscillation coloring—is solved; iteration 2 confirmed that DFS timestamps (O(n) precomputation) are a strict improvement over all-pairs BFS (O(n²)) while producing identical round counts on all 20 test cases.
key_points: SCORE ACHIEVED: 100/100 with perfect 3/3 consistency using DFS timestamps + array-based adjacency + compiler pragmas. This is the maximum possible score.

KEY FINDING CONFIRMED: DFS subtree-membership checks are mathematically equivalent to BFS distance comparisons for tree routing, eliminating the 2MB distance matrix and O(n²) precomputation while producing identical swap schedules on all 20 test cases.

ABLATION VALIDATED: Array-based adjacency lists are critical—switching to std::vector drops score to 94-99 (mean 96.03) due to cache misses in the per-round DP loop (~2000 rounds × ~500 nodes) AND incompatibility with AVX2 vectorization pragmas.

FAILED ALTERNATIVES CATALOGUED: Edge-index coloring (catastrophic on bushy trees, 6x round budget), endgame relaxation (oscillation on bushy trees), int distance matrix (cache pressure → score 95). Depth-parity 2-coloring is the correct anti-oscillation scheme for bipartite tree structure.

WHAT'S LEFT TO EXPLORE: (1) Whether simpler code could achieve 100 via better algorithmic round counts rather than implementation optimization; (2) cycle-decomposition approaches that might reduce from ~2n to ~1.5n rounds on bushy trees; (3) adaptive root selection. However, since the score is already maxed at 100, further iterations offer no score improvement on this problem instance.

RECOMMENDATION: The problem is solved at maximum score. A third iteration would only be valuable for scientific understanding (e.g., tighter round-count bounds), not for score improvement. Suggest concluding the campaign.
